literal: He who knows by himself what is painful to his own life, why indeed does he do painful things to other abiding lives?
translation: How can a person, who knows from personal experience the pain inflicted on their own life, inflict pain on other living beings?
modern: தன் உயிருக்குத் துன்பம் தருவது எது என்று தான் அனுபவித்து அறிந்தவன், மற்ற எளிய உயிர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் செய்ய நினைப்பது ஏனோ?
explanation: This couplet establishes empathy as the foundation of non-injury. A person knows firsthand what causes pain and suffering to their own self ('தன்னுயிர்க்கு இன்னாமை'). Having this direct, personal knowledge ('தான் அறிவான்'), it is incomprehensible ('என்கொலோ') why they would still choose to inflict similar suffering on other living creatures ('மன்னுயிர்க்கு இன்னா செயல்'). The word 'மன்னுயிர்' refers to the abiding, vulnerable lives of other living beings in the world. The poet uses a rhetorical question to urge the reader to use their own capacity for feeling pain as a guide to avoid harming others.
